The University Hospital Essen offers first class medical services in the Ruhr metropolis. Every year, 225.000 patients are treated in 30 clinics, 27 institutes and specialized centers. The over 8.000 employees offer medical care with state-of-the-art diagnosis and therapies, which meet highest international standards. Patient care is connected with basic and translational research at an internationally competitive level.Hemoglobin is best known for its role in oxygen transport in red blood cells. Our preliminary findings indicate that it is also expressed by lung immune cells, where it may contribute to antiviral defense. These findings further suggest that the thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1)/CD47 signaling axis limits hemoglobin expression and its associated antiviral antivity.The project aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying hemoglobin-mediated antiviral defense and determine how this response is regulated by TSP-1/CD47 signaling. GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The Research Unit Magmatic and Hydrothermal Systems (MuHS) of the research division 4 - Dynamics of the Ocean Floor is offering a position preferably starting as soon as possible. The position offers the possibility to attain a doctoral degree in natural sciences.The position is within the framework of the project “Understanding Core-Mantle Interaction Through Global Mapping of Ultra-Low Velocity Zones in Mantle Convection Models”, which is part of the German Science Foundation's Priority Programm SPP 2404 DeepDyn (https://www.geo.lmu.de/deepdyn/en/) about reconstructing the deep dynamics of planet Earth over geologic time.Ultra-Low Velocity Zones (ULVZs) are thin patches at the base of Earth’s mantle-only tens of kilometres high yet 100 to 1000 km wide-where seismic shear waves exhibit extreme reductions of 20-30%. They are archives of Earth’s thermochemical evolution, potentially reflecting its early differentiation or interactions with the core, but also more recent mantle flow patterns. Yet these interpretations depend critically on ULVZ composition, which remains poorly constrained.The doctoral researcher will numerically model ULVZ evolution and properties in plate-guided global mantle convection simulations. They will develop a framework that quantitatively evaluates these simulations by inferring ULVZ properties from mineral physics and comparing them to seismic constraints, including ULVZ geometry, geographic location and distribution. They will synthesize these results to deliver the first global ULVZ map based on dynamic simulations and to discriminate among proposed ULVZ compositions. The German Diabetes Center (DDZ), Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU) Düsseldorf is an interdisciplinary research institute that links basic and clinical sciences to improve prevention, diagnosis and therapy of Diabetes mellitus and its complications. The Junior Research Group Crosstalk (head: Dr. Melanie Mittenbühler) at the Institute for Clinical Biochemistry and Pathobiochemistry focuses on how inter-tissue communication impacts energy balance and metabolic health. We are seeking a talented and highly motivatedPostdoctoral Fellow (PhD/Dr. rer. nat., m/f/div., E13 TV-L 100%) to join our research group. Our group investigates how skeletal muscle acts as an endocrine organ and communicates with other tissues through secreted signaling molecules, particularly myokines. In the ERC Starting Grant project MYOSCAN, we systematically investigate how exercise and age-related muscle loss alter the skeletal muscle secretome. We aim to identify novel exercise-sensitive myokines and define their roles in sarcopenia, metabolic disease, and cancer biology. A central question is whether muscle-derived factors promote or suppress tumor growth and how these signaling pathways can be therapeutically targeted.PhD in molecular biology, cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, exercise science, metabolism, cancer biology, or a related fieldStrong expertise in at least one of the following areas: proteomics/mass spectrometry, secretome analysis, cell biology, molecular signaling, metabolic research, or cancer biology. jobs.occupation: Senior Global Pricing and Access Manager Immuno-Oncology (m/w/d) (Leiter/in - Marketing)
jobs.employer_name: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description: OUR COMPANYAt Boehringer Ingelheim we develop breakthrough therapies and innovative healthcare solutions in areas of unmet medical need for both humans and animals. As a family owned company, we focus on long-term performance. We believe that, if we have talented and ambitious people who are passionate about innovation, there is no limit to what we can achieve; after all, we started with just 28 people. Now, we are powered by 50,000 employees globally who nurture a diverse, collaborative and inclusive culture.The PositionAt Boehringer Ingelheim, we are committed to delivering breakthrough therapies that have an unprecedented impact for people facing cancer, today and for generations to come. This high-impact global role contributes to our early oncology pipeline, where payer confidence, evidence quality, development and launch sequencing, and pricing strategy can shape how quickly innovation reaches patients. As (Senior) Global Pricing and Access Manager, you will help define the access ambition for early pipeline products and translate science, payer expectations, competitive dynamics and country realities into clear strategic choices. You will work closely with Global Access, HEOR, Medical, Clinical Development, Regulatory, Commercial, Forecasting, Finance, and regional and local teams to ensure payer needs are embedded in evidence generation, value communication, pricing decisions, and launch planning from the beginning.Tasks & responsibilities- In this role, you will drive the development and execution of global pricing and access strategies for early immuno-oncology assets across current and future indications, ensuring payer considerations are integrated into asset and indication planning.- With a focus on value creation, you will develop and refine payer value propositions by translating clinical, economic and market evidence into compelling value narratives.- As part of a cross-functional environment, you will lead payer-relevant evidence planning in partnership with HEOR, Medical and Clinical colleagues, identifying evidence needs, risks and opportunities.- By providing strategic guidance, you will develop global pricing recommendations that support launch planning, lifecycle management, indication expansion and long-term value optimization.- When evaluating market dynamics, you will lead the generation and interpretation of payer, HTA, reimbursement and competitive insights, translating findings into actionable recommendations.- Within your area of responsibility, you will drive access launch readiness across regions and markets, ensuring global strategies and value communications are effectively translated into local implementation.- Through close collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, you will ensure payer and access perspectives are reflected in development, evidence and commercialization planning.Requirements- Graduate degree in Medicine, Life Sciences, Health Economics, Pharmacy, Business, Finance, or a related discipline.- Long term experience in the pharmaceutical industry in Oncology with a strong background in Immuno-oncology market access, pricing, reimbursement or payer authority roles- Demonstrated experience supporting global pricing and access strategy development for Immuno-oncology assets, ideally during pre-launch or launch-phase planning.- Deep understanding of global healthcare systems across major markets and the ability to adapt strategies to market-specific requirements.- Proven ability to independently lead complex cross-functional market access initiatives and translate ambiguity into clear recommendations and actionable plans.- Fluent English communication, presentation and stakeholder engagement skills.As part of our commitment to transparency and fairness, salary information will be shared during the recruitment process. We also offer a comprehensive benefits and wellbeing package.Applications from persons with severe disabilities are warmly welcomed. In cases of equal qualifications, such applicants will be given preferential consideration in the selection process.With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better.Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed.Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations.Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.comReady to contact us?If you have any questions about the job posting or process - please contact our HR Direct Team, Tel: +49 (0) 6132 77-3330 or via mail: hr.de@boehringer-ingelheim.comRecruitment process:Step 1: Online application - The job posting is presumably online until November 19th, 2026. We reserve the right to take the posting offline beforehand. Applications up to November 12th, 2026 are guaranteed to be considered.Step 2: Virtual meeting in the period from end November till Mid of DecemberStep 3: On-site interviews beginning of January
